description: Return the public profile of one catalog project, identified either by host and an owner/repo slug or a numeric repository id, or by registry and package, a package name on a package registry. host and exactly one of slug or id are required unless registry and package are given; a call missing them, giving both slug and id, or giving a host other than github or gitlab or a slug that is a URL or ends in a slash is refused as an invalid argument and names what is wrong. registry and package are given together and without host, slug or id. registry accepts only the package registries this catalog admits, currently npm; any other value is refused as an invalid argument and the refusal names the accepted values. package must be a well-formed npm package name, such as commander or @scope/name; a malformed name is refused as an invalid argument. A package resolves only when it is bound to a repository both ways: the repository's package.json names the npm package, and the package names the repository as its source. The package.json is the repository's root one unless it is marked private, or one in a workspace package directory; a package named only by a workspace package.json binds once its first stable release that names the repository is at least 90 days old and every stable release that names a repository names this one. A verified signed publish attestation for the package's newest stable version that names the repository also binds it, under the same age rule. A package that is not bound to a project is not found, and so is a package bound to more than one project. A well-formed lookup that matches no project is not an error: it returns {"found": false, "meaning": "not-in-catalog"} with a fixed note. The catalog covers only part of the JavaScript and TypeScript ecosystem and does not yet hold every project published to npm, so a not-found result says nothing about whether the repository exists or about its health. This resolves any project the catalog holds, including one below the discovery floor that search does not return. A project on gitlab is published with its health signals unavailable, so search_projects does not return it and compare_projects refuses it; get_project is the one tool that returns it. A former slug recorded in a project's slug_history resolves to that project, returned under its current slug; a slug that is the current slug of a project resolves to that project first. The profile carries the claim state, verification or generation provenance, the vocabulary dimensions (category, ecosystem, kind, runtime, license_family, topics and capabilities, each present only when it has a value), the five health-signal bands, license and package-registry facets, and staleness. facets.registry_link is on every profile and says how a registry package relates to the project: bound when a package and the repository name each other, so the package's data is used; unverified when a package names the repository but it isn't verified as this repository's package, so none of the package's data is used and the package is not named; not-found when no package is known to name the repository. It also carries ranking_state: ranked when the project is among the ranked projects that search_projects lists for a call with filters and no query; settling when it is at or above the discovery floor but in the settling hold, so search returns it only for a call with a query; and below_floor when it is below the discovery floor, so search does not return it. ranking_state is absent when the project's ranking has not yet been computed. Health signals are reported as bands, not raw measures; no person-derived counts are included. What each band means, and its cut-point, is published on the catalog's methodology page (/methodology) and returned by get_methodology. Read-only. Serves catalog schema v1.

host.description: Repository host, e.g. "github". Required with slug or id.

id.description: The numeric repository id (the stable identity anchor).

package.description: A package name on registry, e.g. "commander" or "@scope/name". Resolves only when the package is bound to the repository both ways.

registry.description: A package registry this catalog admits. Given with package, and without host, slug or id.

name: get_project
